questions.question:
Q1. If sinA = 5/13 , cosB = 4/5 Find
  a) sin (A + B) = (2 marks)
  b) cos (A – B) (2 marks)
  c) cosn2A (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Taking A and B as acute angles: cosA = 12/13, sinB = 3/5.
a) sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB = (5/13)(4/5) + (12/13)(3/5) = 20/65 + 36/65 = 56/65
b) cos(A – B) = cosA cosB + sinA sinB = (12/13)(4/5) + (5/13)(3/5) = 48/65 + 15/65 = 63/65
c) (read as cos 2A) cos2A = 1 – 2sin²A = 1 – 2(25/169) = 119/169

questions.section: PART TWO : Structured Questions. (60 Marks)
questions.question:
Q2.
  a) Solve the equation for 0 ≤ x ≤ 180
     2cos² x – √3 cosx = 0 (3 marks)
  b) Prove that
     (1 – sin²θ)/cosθ = 1/secθ (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) cosx(2cosx – √3) = 0
   cosx = 0 → x = 90°
   cosx = √3/2 → x = 30°
   Solutions: x = 30°, 90°
b) LHS = (1 – sin²θ)/cosθ = cos²θ/cosθ = cosθ = 1/secθ = RHS ∎

questions.section: PART TWO : Structured Questions. (60 Marks)
questions.question:
Q8. The equation of the parabola is x² + 6x – 8y + 17 = 0
   Find
  a) The vertex (2 marks)
  b) The focus (2 marks)
  c. The directrix (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Complete the square: (x + 3)² – 9 – 8y + 17 = 0 → (x + 3)² = 8(y – 1), so 4p = 8, p = 2 (opens upward)
a) Vertex = (–3, 1)
b) Focus = (–3, 1 + 2) = (–3, 3)
c) Directrix: y = 1 – 2 → y = –1
